restart_api_pool.detail: Restarting catalog-api workers dropped CPU to ~40% for 25 seconds; the same v5.2.0 build was still deployed and CPU returned to 97% within 30 seconds.
restart_api_pool.lesson: Restarting catalog-api gave a 25 second CPU dip and then regression; the leaking code path was still deployed.
restart_api_pool.reusable_lesson: Restarting catalog-api workers during an N+1 CPU saturation incident only resets the symptom for ~25 seconds: CPU fell from 97% to 41% and then returned to 97% on the same build. Roll back the code path instead.

rollback_recent_deploy.detail: Rolled back to v5.1.4, restoring the ProductVariant prefetch. CPU 31%, queries/min 940, category page p95 230ms.
rollback_recent_deploy.lesson: The deploy was the cause, so the rollback was the fix.
rollback_recent_deploy.reusable_lesson: For catalog-api CPU saturation with an N+1 shape, rolling back the serializer release restores CPU and page latency within two minutes. Confirm with queries-per-request before and after.

scale_out_workers.detail: Adding 10 workers multiplied the query storm: postgres-catalog CPU hit 100%, DB latency 2.4s, and page latency got worse (14s).
scale_out_workers.lesson: Scaling out a CPU-bound service moves the load to the database and makes the incident worse.
scale_out_workers.reusable_lesson: Never scale out catalog-api during an N+1 CPU incident: 10 extra workers pushed postgres-catalog to 100% CPU and page latency from 8.9s to 14s. Fix the query shape first.

kill_long_running_queries.detail: Killing long queries freed some connections but the storm refilled them within seconds; CPU and latency were unchanged because the problem is query count, not query duration.
kill_long_running_queries.lesson: Connection-level mitigation does nothing for a query-count problem.
kill_long_running_queries.reusable_lesson: Killing long-running queries did not help the catalog-api N+1 incident: the failure is query volume, not query duration. Roll back the change that created the per-item queries.

add_index.detail: A covering index cut per-item query cost by ~9x and CPU fell to 58%, but the N+1 shape remains, so this is a mitigation with a follow-up required.
add_index.lesson: Indexing reduces the cost per query but not the number of queries; the leak shape is still there.
add_index.reusable_lesson: A covering index reduces the impact of the catalog-api N+1 incident (CPU 97% -> 58%) but does not remove the per-item query pattern; prefer the rollback, or land the index together with the prefetch fix.

flush_cache.detail: HIGH RISK: flushing the catalog cache would drop a warm cache and send every request to the database, making the query storm worse. Blocked by the safety gate.
flush_cache.lesson: Cache flush during a database-bound incident is actively harmful.
flush_cache.reusable_lesson: Flushing the catalog cache during an N+1 incident doubles the database load (queries/min 41k -> 74k) because a warm cache is protecting the database. Never flush a cache that is shielding a saturated datastore.
